readme_for_ai: Machine-readable list of every dataset used to train or test the Aegex IoT intrusion-detection models (LSTM autoencoder, VAE, temporal GAT). One object per dataset in `datasets`. Fields: `url` = download page (Kaggle unless host = zenodo); `kaggle_slug` = argument for `kaggle datasets download -d <slug>`; `files` = exact file names (`used` false = downloaded/available but not used; `sha256` = checksum of the original file, null if it was never downloaded to the project PC); `adapter` = code that converts it; `labelling` = how the dataset's own labels were mapped to the project classes; `operations` = every processing step applied, in order; `used_by_models` = model runs that used it. Originals were never modified. Project attack classes: benign, scanning, ddos, mirai, ransomware, other (other = out of scope, never a training target). Human-readable detail: DATASETS_AND_PREPROCESSING.md in this folder.
where_to_put_files: all original files in one folder, then set environment variable AEGEX_DATA to it (Gotham zip in <AEGEX_DATA>/gotham_2025/); outputs go to AEGEX_OUT
shared_operations: step1_flows: adapter -> unified flow table (or packets -> bidirectional flows via FlowBuilder: inactivity timeout 300 s TCP / 60 s UDP-ICMP-ARP, 120 s active timeout, IPv4 + ARP only)

step2_features: 50 features per flow (17 numeric incl. 4 device-behaviour, 33 binary); chronological split per (capture, attack_class) 70 % train / 15 % val / 15 % test; RobustScaler per dataset fitted on train + clean benign flows only; hosts that send attack traffic marked device_compromised

step3_sequences_graphs: per-device windows of 32 flows, stride 16; 60 s graph snapshots (nodes = hosts, edges = host pairs, mean features + log flow count, single-peer public IPs merged into EXTERNAL)
